name: Lake Tulpar-Kul
near: Sary-Mogol — about 25 km to the northwest (Visit Alay, Backpack Adventures); the base for transfers, horses and CBT. It can also be reached on horseback from Kashka-Suu (too.kg).
elev: About 3500 m (too.kg; at the yurt camp — sarymogol.com). Visit Alay's claim of “the same altitude as the base camp” is not accepted as an exact figure.
short: Tulpar-Kul is a high-mountain lake (~3500 m) in the Alay Valley, within easy reach of Lenin Peak base camp (7134 m), with yurt camps on its shore.
desc: Tulpar-Kul (Tulpar-Kol) is a fairly large, clear lake at about 3500 m at the foot of the Trans-Alay range, within easy reach of Achyk-Tash, the base camp of Lenin Peak (too.kg). In calm weather Lenin Peak (7134 m) is reflected in it. The lake is 25 km from the village of Sary-Mogol: about 45 min by car, 4–5 h on horseback or 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay). In summer, yurt camps run by CBT and private owners operate on the shore (from 1000 som a night with breakfast and dinner — Visit Alay). Day treks start from the lake to Travellers Pass (~4100 m) and to the tongue of the Lenin glacier, and multi-day ones to Yukhin Peak and Razdelnaya (Visit Alay, CBT). The area is in the border zone — a permit is needed (Visit Alay).
guide: Come to the lake early in the morning: in calm conditions Lenin Peak is reflected in the water, and after lunch the weather in the Trans-Alay often turns bad (TripAdvisor reviews). Spend the night in a yurt on the shore — from 1000 som with dinner and breakfast (Visit Alay) — and the next day climb Travellers Pass (~4100 m): 3 h up, 2 h down and a panorama of the entire Lenin wall. Don't forget your border permit — processing takes 10–20 days (Visit Alay). If you happen to be there on the third weekend of July, Sary-Mogol holds a festival of horse and yak games.
see: The reflection of Lenin Peak (7134 m) in the lake; the wall of the Trans-Alay range; Achyk-Tash base camp nearby; the trek to Travellers Pass (~4100 m) and to the Lenin glacier; marmots in the meadows (too.kg, Visit Alay, TripAdvisor).
skip: You can't get the border permit in time (10–20 days). You tolerate altitude poorly — spending a night at ~3500 m without acclimatization is hard. A view of Lenin Peak from the highway near Sary-Tash is enough for you.
diff: The lake itself is easy: you can drive right to the shore. Treks: Travellers Pass — 3 h up/2 h down to ~4100 m (Visit Alay); the trek to the glacier is ~14 km, with passes up to 3820 m, moderate (CBT); Yukhin Peak 2–3 days, Razdelnaya 4–5 days with equipment (Visit Alay).
when: June — September (CBT); the yurt camps operate only in summer, the trekking season runs from late May — June; from October the risk of snow grows (Backpack Adventures). The festival of horse and yak games is on the third weekend of July (Visit Alay). I Love KG: best time June–August, the yurt camps close in September.
hours: A natural area, accessible round the clock (TripAdvisor: 00:00–23:59); the yurt camps operate in the summer season (Backpack Adventures). A border permit is needed (Visit Alay).
daytime: Early morning — calm air and the reflection of Lenin Peak; the weather becomes unpredictable toward evening (TripAdvisor reviews).
how: From Osh to Sary-Mogol (~4 h, CBT): a marshrutka (minibus) from the Osh bus station at 14:00, arriving around 18:00, 300 som; a shared taxi from the new bus station 400 som/seat; a private car 3000 som (Backpack Adventures; the 14:00 departure is confirmed by the schedule of 27.08.2026 — I Love KG). The distance Osh — Sary-Mogol is ~220 km, about 4 h of pure driving (I Love KG). From Sary-Mogol it is 25 km to the yurt camp by the lake: ~45 min–1 h by car (Visit Alay, CBT), 4–5 h on horseback or 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
needcar: Yes: to Sary-Mogol — marshrutka (minibus)/taxi; from Sary-Mogol to the lake — a CBT/private car (1500 som per car), a horse, or an 8–9 h walk.
self: Yes, with a border permit: marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to Sary-Mogol, then a CBT car or on foot; you can pitch a tent for free in designated places (Visit Alay).
roadtype: Osh — Sary-Tash — Sary-Mogol — paved (the highway via Taldyk); from Sary-Mogol to the lake it is 25 km of dirt road across the Alay Valley with fords, passable for cars/SUVs in ~45 min (Visit Alay; surface type — editorial, based on descriptions).
traveltime: Osh → Sary-Mogol ~4 h (CBT; marshrutka 14:00–18:00); Sary-Mogol → lake ~45 min–1 h by car (Visit Alay, CBT), 4–5 h on horseback, 8–9 h on foot (Visit Alay).
stay: Yurt camps on the shore: from 1000 som/night with breakfast and dinner (Visit Alay; Backpack Adventures); the CBT Sary-Mogol yurt camp “Tulpor-Kul” — warm yurts by the shore, a stove, lighting, a shared toilet and shower outside the yurts (CBT, sarymogol.com); one TripAdvisor review advises choosing an alternative to the CBT camp. Tents — free in designated places. In Sary-Mogol — guesthouses at $15–20 with breakfast (Backpack Adventures). Prices according to reports: CBT camp 1000 som ($15) per bed with dinner and breakfast (Nature's Off Grid Treasures) / $30 with three meals (The Gone Goat); a tent pitch on the camp grounds $8–10; dinner 300 som, breakfast 250 som.
net: Specific Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage at the lake is not confirmed in 2025–2026 sources. The Lenin Peak base camps (Achyk-Tash, ~10 km) have “3G WiFi” (The Gone Goat); in Sary-Mogol Wi-Fi is unreliable, and a local SIM is advised (Backpack Adventures). Expect no signal at the lake itself.
entry: There is no entrance ticket. Border permit: ≈$35–40 via Visit Alay (FAQ 07.2026) or 2054 som (Nature's Off Grid Treasures), 1–3 weeks to process; for the lake itself it may formally not be required (see the warning).
transfer: Osh → Sary-Mogol: marshrutka (minibus) 300 som, shared taxi 400 som/seat, private car 3000 som; Sary-Mogol → Tulpar-Kul 1500 som per car one way (Backpack Adventures, Visit Alay; 2023–2025 data, check). An alternative from The Gone Goat's report: a shared taxi Osh → Sary-Mogol 500 som/seat (3 h), a driver to Tulpar-Kul 500–800 som.
bring: Warm clothes and a down jacket (nights at 3500 m are cold even in summer), sun protection and sunglasses, your passport and border permit, cash in som (an ATM in Sary-Mogol was open in 2023 — economist.kg), trekking shoes, a first-aid kit including altitude-sickness remedies.
warn: Border permit: Visit Alay (FAQ, updated 12.07.2026) — a permit is mandatory for Lenin Peak base camp; people often go to Tulpar-Kul without it, but Visit Alay strongly advises getting one (≈$35–40, 1–2 weeks) because of military patrols. Nature's Off Grid Treasures — no permit is needed for Tulpar-Kul and Travellers Pass, but military checks are possible (permit 2054 som, 10–20 days); The Gone Goat — no checks were encountered. I Love KG (2026) — not needed for the highway and Sary-Mogol, needed for Achyk-Tash. Conclusion: formally the lake is on the edge of the border zone — it is safer to get a permit. Altitude ~3500 m: risk of altitude sickness. The weather changes toward evening (TripAdvisor). Fords on the way from Sary-Mogol can be deep after rain (editorial).
food: Dinner and breakfast at the yurt camp (included in the 1000 som — Visit Alay): Kyrgyz home cooking, kumis from shepherds in summer; in Sary-Mogol — meals at guesthouses (editorial).
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 38 ratings (03.10.2026); TripAdvisor: 4.7/5, 9 reviews, no. 1 of 3 in Sary-Mogol (reviews 07.2018–07.2025). Pros: views of Lenin Peak, treks of varying difficulty, yurts on the shore, marmots; cons: unpredictable weather after lunch, uneven quality of the camps (one review against the CBT camp).
p.sum: From Osh take a marshrutka (minibus) or shared taxi to Sary-Mogol (220 km, 4–5 h; marshrutka at 14:00 from the New Bus Station, 300 som), spend the night in a guesthouse, and in the morning take a CBT car to the lake (23–25 km, ~45 min–1 h, 1500–2000 som per car) or ride on horseback for 4–5 h. On the shore are yurt camps run by CBT, Buaisha and others (1000–2000 som with dinner and breakfast; $30 with three meals), season ~late June — early September. The main walk is Travellers Pass (4150 m, 16 km round trip, 5–8 h). A permit is formally needed for Achyk-Tash; people often go to the lake without one, but it is safer to get it.

p.iti.0.title: Minimum (2 days from Osh)
p.iti.0.plan: Day 1: 14:00 marshrutka (minibus) from the New Bus Station → ~18:30 Sary-Mogol, night in a guesthouse. Day 2: 08:00 a CBT car to the lake (1 h), a walk around the lake, back by lunchtime; there is almost no public transport back the same day — 3 days is better.
p.iti.1.title: 3–4 days (recommended)
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Osh — Sary-Mogol. Day 2: a car to Tulpar-Kul, an acclimatization walk to Achyk-Tash (2.5 h), night in a yurt. Day 3: Travellers Pass (5–8 h), night in a yurt. Day 4: on foot/by car to Sary-Mogol and a shared taxi to Osh.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Taldyk Pass and Sary-Tash on the way; further — Kozhokelen, the Kosh-Kol lakes, the Sary-Mogol — Jiptik trek; the Pamir Highway to Kyzyl-Art (Tajikistan, GBAO permit).
p.season: May — snow on Taldyk, the camps are closed; late June — early September — the yurt camps operate (The Gone Goat: 25.06–05.09); July — peak, the horse games festival on the third weekend of July; August — the best weather, thunderstorms after lunch; September — the camps close, nights below zero; October–April — snow, only Sary-Mogol.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka (minibus) 300 + 300 som (round trip) + a car to the lake 1500–2000 som/car (≈500 per person in a group of 4) + a guesthouse $15 + a yurt 1000–1300 som with half board → ~4000–5000 som/person for 3 days
p.budget.comfort: Tripster jeep tour 3 days $390/person (group of 4); or a transfer $150 per car Osh — Tulpar + an Ak-Sai yurt $75–85; permit ~$35–40
p.permits: Achyk-Tash and Lenin Peak base camp — border zone, a permit is mandatory (Visit Alay FAQ 07.2026, I Love KG 2026). People often go to Tulpar-Kul itself without a permit, and there is no checkpoint (The Gone Goat 2024, Beyond Wild Places), but military checks are possible — it is safer to get one. How: via CBT Sary-Mogol or Visit Alay (~$35–40, 1–2 weeks) or on your own via tour.too.kg (3000 som, 5–7 working days, office at 105/3 Isanov St.); The Gone Goat/Visit Alay state 10–20 days.
p.access: With children — yes by car to the camp (Tripster lists it as suitable for families), but at 3500 m be careful with little ones; for older people — only by car and after acclimatization; with a stroller — no (dirt ground, yurts); with a dog — possible, but there are shepherd dogs and livestock nearby.
